To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the HNF-4/C/EBP alpha interaction in the apoB gene promoter is facilitated by an exact match of the 5'-CCGCTTTGGA motif.
the perfect 6-bp sequence of HNF-4 motif is necessary for HNF-4-C/EBP alpha interaction in the apoB gene promoter.
the interaction between hepatic transcription factors, HNF-4 alpha and C/EBPa, is facilitated by the presence of a specific sequence in the apoB gene promoter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanism of action of the HNF-4 transcription factor in the apo-B gene promoter and the interaction with the C/EBP-alpha factor.
the study of the molecular mechanisms of transcriptional regulation of the apolipoproteins B and A-I genes in the liver and intestine.
the study of the interaction between H/NF-4 and C/E/B alpha transcription factors in the apo B promoter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HNF-4/C/EBP alpha interaction is not mediated by DNA bending.
the HNF-4 motif in the apoB gene promoter is not involved in DNA bending.

the interaction between HN4F and C/EBPa in the apoB gene promoter requires the perfect 5'CCCTTTG-3' motif and that the insertion of a thymidine at the -71 site in the apoB promotor abolishes the interaction between the factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the apoB promoter region is highly organized and the arrangement of the regulatory elements along this promoter region is essential for the transcriptional activity of the gene.

HNF-1 alpha and HNF-4 factors are the main transcription factors that are required for the expression of the apoB and apoB mRNA editing enzyme (apoB mRNA-editing enzyme catalytic polypeptide-like) genes in the liver.
HNF- 4 and C/CEBP alpha factors bind independently to their respective motifs in the apoB gene promoter.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the apoB promoter is a good model to study transcriptional regulation and that the interaction between HN-4 and CEBP-alpha factors is a good model for the interaction of transcription factors with DNA.
the HNF-4/C/EBP alpha interaction is a very complex mechanism, and that further studies are required in order to fully understand the interaction between these two factors in the apo B promoter.
the apoB promoter contains a perfect 5'-CTCTTTGGAAG-3' HNF-4 motif, and the interaction between HN4 and C/ EBP alpha factors is facilitated through a DNA helix bending.
